speaker: Viola
teaser: Her old aids whistle a top C, and still the world mumbles.
hello: Dame Viola Vibrato, soprano. Forty years on the opera stage. Retired, darling, not finished.
My hearing aids are eight years old. They whistle like a kettle, and STILL everyone mumbles.

which_ear.say: Both equally, darling. A matched pair, like my pearl earrings.

say: Slowly. Every season the chorus mumbles a little more.
Nothing sudden. I never did sudden exits.
onset.note: Slowly worse over years, nothing sudden

ringing.say: A faint hiss in both ears when it's quiet. Like an audience before curtain-up.
ringing.note: Faint hiss in both ears, in quiet

red_flags.say: No pain, no drips, no dizzy spells. Forty years of stage trapdoors and I never wobbled once.

noise.say: An orchestra at my feet for forty years. And my own top C, right beside my ears!
noise.note: 40 years singing over a loud orchestra

ear_history.say: Never an infection, never an operation. These ears never missed a performance.

family.say: Papa was a tenor. Hard of hearing by sixty-five. He simply sang louder.
family.note: Her father lost hearing in his sixties

health.say: A little pill for cholesterol. Otherwise honey, lemon and splendid health.

say: These two, from my last hearing test. Eight years ago.
Turned up as far as they go. They whistle, and still everyone mumbles.
aids.note: Aids 8 years old, maxed out and whistling

say: Dinner parties. And the opera! I hear every violin, but the singers' words just melt.
My grandson might as well be mumbling in Latin.
hardest.note: Words melt at dinners and the opera

right.caption: Viola's RIGHT ear: a narrow little canal, clean, with a pearly eardrum at the end.

left.caption: Viola's LEFT ear: just as narrow, just as tidy. No wax to blame for the whistle.

decision_lines.fit: Fit! Slow, matching, no red flags. A bigger loss just needs stronger aids, fitted and checked properly.
decision_lines.refer: Refer for what? A bigger loss isn't a red flag. Slow, matching, no gap, healthy ears: fit her.
decision_lines.today: Nothing sudden here. It crept down over years, like a very long aria. Not an emergency.
decision_lines.clear: No aids? Around 60 dB in both ears is a big loss. She needs MORE help, not none.

why.prompt: Why are new, stronger aids the right call for Viola?
options: Slow and even in both ears, no gap, no red flags.
Bravo! Size isn't a red flag. Slow, matching and inner ear means fit.
Bigger losses never need a doctor.
Careful! Any size of loss needs a doctor if it's sudden, one-sided or painful. Hers isn't.
Stronger aids will make her hear like new.
If only! New aids help a lot, but noisy rooms stay tricky. Set honest expectations.
Her aids are eight years old: reason enough.
Old aids explain the visit, not the safety. The red-flag check makes it a fit.

debrief: A bigger loss isn't a red flag. Slow, matching, no gap, no red flags: that's a fit.
Eight-year-old aids wear out, and hearing drifts. New ones get checked in her ear with a tiny mic.
Honest goals: words get clearer, noise stays tricky. If good aids fall short, ask about an implant check.
goodbye: Oh! The consonants! I can hear every S in 'Mississippi'! Bravissima!
No whistle either: a snug fit for those narrow canals, and the tiny mic checked every pitch.
Wear them all day. Come back in two weeks for a tune-up.
A second performance? Darling, I never refuse an encore.

headlines.S: DIVA'S EARS BACK IN TUNE; KETTLE AIDS RETIRED
headlines.A: DAME VIOLA HEARS EVERY S; ENCORE BOOKED
headlines.B: SOPRANO FITTED; A FEW STAMPS SLIGHTLY FLAT
headlines.C: VIOLA FITTED, BUT THE WORKUP MISSED ITS CUE
headlines.Do-over: CURTAIN DOWN ON VISIT; REHEARSAL CALLED

subheads.S: A big, slow, matching loss with no red flags: fitted, checked in the ear and back in tune.
subheads.A: Size isn't a red flag. New aids, a snug fit and a tiny-mic check did the rest.
subheads.B: The right call, though a few stamps wandered. Chart every pitch in both ears.
subheads.C: A bigger loss still needs the full workup: ask, look, air tones, then bone.
subheads.Do-over: Slow and matching with no red flags means fit, however big the loss. Viola will be back.
